actions.reason: Both classes denote segmentation of retinal blood vessels in medical images and share the same parent; ‘retinal vessels’ in this context effectively means blood vessels, so the more concise and commonly used label is chosen as canonical.

comment: The two classes describe the same medical image segmentation task (retinal blood vessel/vessel segmentation) with identical parent type and no distinguishable scope difference, so they should be merged using RetinalVesselSegmentation as the canonical class and treating RetinalBloodVesselSegmentation as an alias.

actions.reason: An ActiveLearningStrategy is a specific way of guiding or instantiating the general ActiveLearning methodology, so it is conceptually narrower and should be modeled as a subclass of ActiveLearning rather than as a separate synonym.

comment: ActiveLearning denotes the overall methodology/process, while ActiveLearningStrategy denotes concrete strategic variants that guide how active learning is conducted. They are not synonyms; ActiveLearningStrategy should be modeled as a subclass of ActiveLearning to form a clear hierarchy.

actions.reason: Represents a meta-level taxonomy/organizational construct rather than a concrete active learning method; keeping only the method class yields a cleaner, more reusable ontology. The taxonomy concept is mis-modeled as an ActiveLearningMethod and is better handled via annotation or external classification schemes rather than as a separate OWL class.

comment: The two classes describe different levels: a concrete family of active learning methods vs. a taxonomy that categorizes such methods. To keep the ontology focused on domain entities and avoid meta-level container classes, deprecate RepresentativenessBasedActiveLearningTaxonomy and retain RepresentativenessBasedActiveLearning as the canonical class for representativeness-based methods.

actions.reason: Both classes describe the same concept: selecting/forming batches of queries per iteration in batch-mode active learning; the distinction between 'algorithms' and 'procedures' is not ontologically meaningful here. Chosen canonical name aligns with the parent class BatchModeActiveLearning.

comment: BatchModeQuerySelection and BatchQuerySelection both denote the batch query selection mechanism in batch-mode active learning and share the same parent. They should be merged, with BatchModeQuerySelection kept as the canonical class for naming consistency and BatchQuerySelection treated as an alias.

actions.reason: Both classes describe density-based selection procedures for active learning and share the same parent; the only difference is wording (“Acquisition” vs “AcquisitionMethod”), so they should be treated as a single concept aligned with the ontology’s *AcquisitionMethod naming pattern.

comment: The two classes are near-synonyms under DensityBasedActiveLearning, differing only by inclusion of the word “Method”. They do not form a meaningful hierarchy; merging into DensityBasedAcquisitionMethod preserves consistency with other *AcquisitionMethod classes.

actions.reason: CoreSetActiveLearningMethod describes concrete algorithmic instances of the more general concept CoreSetActiveLearning (active learning methods based on core-set selection), so it should be modeled as a subclass rather than a separate parallel class.

comment: CoreSetActiveLearning is the general concept of core-set based active learning, while CoreSetActiveLearningMethod explicitly denotes concrete algorithmic implementations. This supports a meaningful parent–child hierarchy, with CoreSetActiveLearning as the more general class and CoreSetActiveLearningMethod as its subclass.

actions.reason: Human annotation effort is a specific form or component of overall annotation cost (e.g., time, cognitive load), so it should be modeled as a more specific subclass of the more general AnnotationCost constraint.

comment: AnnotationCost is a general constraint on the cost of annotation, while AnnotationEffort focuses specifically on human effort. These are related but not synonymous; AnnotationEffort is best modeled as a subtype of AnnotationCost rather than a separate, unrelated constraint.

InterAnnotatorVariability and IntraAnnotatorVariability describe two orthogonal, standard distinctions in annotation quality analysis: variability across different annotators vs. variability within a single annotator over time. They are already modeled as sibling subclasses of AnnotationVariabilityConstraint, neither is a synonym or a special case of the other, so both should be kept as distinct classes without merge or deprecation.

The two classes differ along an essential axis (presence vs. absence of labels) and are both already modeled as subclasses of Dataset. Neither is a special case of the other, and they are not synonyms, so they should remain as distinct sibling subclasses without merge or deprecation.

actions.reason: ColonoscopyFrameData represents individual frames derived from colonoscopy videos, making it a more specific dataset type than ColonoscopyVideoData, which represents the full video sequences.

comment: ColonoscopyVideoData is the more general concept (video datasets from colonoscopy), while ColonoscopyFrameData is a specialization for frame-level datasets extracted from those videos. They should be kept in a parent–child hierarchy rather than merged or deprecated.

LabeledDatasetSplit and UnlabeledDatasetSplit represent mutually exclusive sibling concepts (labeled vs. unlabeled portions of a dataset split), both already modeled as subclasses of DataSplit. They are not synonyms and neither is a strict subtype of the other, so both should be kept as distinct classes with no structural changes.
